answer: In an agent economy, require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. This does not make identities unique: an attacker can still create many, but each must tie up capital, and each detected fake destroys part of it. A basalt supply ledger can anchor stake records, while an orchard of auditors checks claims; the kernel is economic accountability, not a claim that names cannot be copied.
